content.user_title: Plan Home Lighting Without Common Mistakes
content.value_statement: Home lighting decisions can create glare, dark zones, wasted spending, or unsafe installations. This skill compares practical options and produces room-specific renovation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Compares main-light and no-main-light layouts for bedrooms, living rooms, kitchens, corridors, and bathrooms.
Explains practical differences between downlights, spotlights, ceiling lights, light strips, and sensor lights.
Recommends color temperature, glare control, fixture placement, and layered lighting based on room use.
Suggests daylighting improvements using windows, glass partitions, doors, curtains, and reflective finishes.
Identifies common renovation mistakes involving lighting, circulation, storage, wet areas, children, and older adults.
Uses 150 Chinese renovation references to provide alternatives, tradeoffs, and planning checklists.
limitations: The source material and default response style are primarily Chinese.
The skill does not perform photometric simulations or verify illuminance measurements.
Advice does not replace a licensed electrician, structural engineer, designer, or local authority.
Regional codes, product specifications, wiring conditions, and site measurements require independent confirmation.

use_cases.title: Plan a First Renovation
use_cases.description: Create a room-by-room lighting checklist before electrical work and fixture purchases begin.

use_cases.title: Review a Lighting Proposal
use_cases.description: Compare a contractor proposal with practical guidance on fixture types, placement, glare, and budget priorities.

use_cases.title: Develop Safer Room Concepts
use_cases.description: Adapt lighting and daylighting choices for kitchens, bathrooms, children, older adults, and low-light rooms.

prompt_templates.title: Plan One Room
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a lighting plan for my [room]. The room is [size], receives [daylight], and has a budget of [budget].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a single room

prompt_templates.title: Compare Fixture Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [option A] and [option B] for my [room]. Explain glare, coverage, installation needs, maintenance, and likely mistakes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Choosing between two fixtures or layouts

prompt_templates.title: Build a Zoned Home Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a zoned lighting plan for this home: [rooms and dimensions]. Prioritize function, color consistency, controls, safety, and budget.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Detailed Proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this lighting proposal: [proposal]. Identify conflicts, missing measurements, glare risks, wiring concerns, code checks, and lower-cost alternatives.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before construction or purchasing

output_examples.input: Plan lighting for a 12-square-meter bedroom used by an older adult.
output: Avoid a dim no-main-light layout with strong contrast.
Use an even ceiling light with dimming and separate bedside task lights.
Choose comfortable controls near the entrance and bed.
Confirm wiring and fixture installation with a licensed electrician.

output_examples.input: Should a small kitchen use spotlights or downlights?
output: Use downlights for even general illumination.
Add focused counter lighting under wall cabinets.
Do not rely on narrow spotlights for the entire kitchen.
Check shadows at the sink, preparation area, and stove.

output_examples.input: Review a living room proposal with glossy tiles and many spotlights.
output: Expect visible reflections and possible glare from glossy flooring.
Reduce unnecessary spotlight groups and keep a clear ambient layer.
Test beam angles and dimming before final installation.
Compare matte or soft-gloss flooring under the proposed fixtures.

best_practices: Provide room dimensions, ceiling height, daylight direction, finishes, users, and budget.
Ask for separate recommendations covering function, atmosphere, controls, safety, and installation checks.
Verify structural changes, wet-area wiring, product ratings, and local rules with qualified professionals.
anti_patterns: Do not request a complete plan without measurements, room use, or budget.
Do not select fixtures only from appearance or social media examples.
Do not treat general guidance as approval for electrical or structural work.

faq.question: Does this skill support no-main-light design?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains suitable rooms, layout choices, cost tradeoffs, glare risks, and cases where a main light is more practical.

faq.question: Can it recommend color temperature?
faq.answer: Yes. Recommendations consider room function, comfort, atmosphere, finish colors, and consistency across connected spaces.

faq.question: Does it cover natural daylight?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests windows, glass partitions, curtains, doors, finishes, and layout changes that may improve daylight.

faq.question: Can it calculate exact lux levels?
faq.answer: No. It can organize requirements, but exact illuminance needs measurements, fixture data, and professional lighting calculations.

faq.question: Is the advice suitable for construction approval?
faq.answer: No. Confirm wiring, wall changes, waterproofing, permits, and local codes with qualified professionals and property management.

faq.question: What information produces the best answer?
faq.answer: Provide dimensions, ceiling height, windows, finishes, furniture layout, users, current wiring, preferred style, and budget.
